text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Wages should be able to sink below the collective agreement level in crisis situations, insolvency expert says. Less qualified workers in the construction and tourism industry should receive less pay.
- Provinces want to negotiate new agreements over working hours for hospital doctors without federal intervention.

- Government-owned Post & Telekom Austria AG is now only negotiating with U.S.-British joint venture Concert on a strategic alliance for data-communication. Previously the firm was in negotiations with Global One and Unisource.
- Austrian ski maker Fischer has already secured 90 percent of its planned turnover with regular orders. High investments in its high-tech unit FACC are planned.
- Some 40 percent of Austrians still do not know who to vote for in Sunday's European parliamentary elections.
- German economic research institute Kieler Institut fuer Weltwirtschaft predicts growth of 1.5 percent for Austria in 1996.
- Because of public spending cuts more private households are failing to pay back loans, study says.

- Police warn of possible bomb attacks ahead of Sunday's elections, similar to one which killed four people last year. Police are tailing 10 suspects, following a threat last week to blow up prominent people in Austria and abroad.
- Linz Textil Holding's profits fell 36.7 percent to 24.1 million schillings in the first half of 1996.
- Austria's Nationalbank will have to pay 800 million schillings more to the European Central Bank for economic and monetary union than it will receive.
- Municipalities will have to reduce their deficits to five billion schillings to meet the Maastricht criteria.
- The information memorandum for the privatisation of the government's stake in Creditanstalt will only be ready by the end of next week.
